method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of the theorem, proof sketch, explanation and index argument; exact formula, macro and identifier parity. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Model-independent normal-form search, primitive-recursive T/U representation, single unbounded search, adopted enumeration and infinitely many indices.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Given descriptions and verifiable computation records, one can search records, test them for f(x), and extract the value. A primitive recursive relation T(e,x,s) and primitive recursive function U(s) represent every partial computable f for some e and every x using least-s search.
samples.checks: The three search steps, quantifier order, partial computable rather than only total computable, and both primitive-recursive claims remain explicit.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: In any chosen model, descriptions and computation sequences can be coded numerically. T recognizes a run code s for index e and input x, and U extracts its result; both can be made primitive recursive. A rigorous proof would fix a model, while many applications need only computability of T and U plus totality of U. Least-s search finds a run and U returns its output when found.
samples.checks: The respective roles of e, x and s, stronger theorem versus weaker application requirements, and undefined search when no record is found are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For the partial-recursive model Kleene used, one unbounded-search operator suffices for a normal form. After fixing suitable T and U, their displayed equation defines the enumeration φ_e. Every partial computable function has infinitely many indices because harmless changes to a description yield distinct indices with the same input-output behavior.
samples.checks: The single-use claim is confined to the stated model, the defining equation and examples 0=0 and counting to 5 remain exact, and index multiplicity is preserved.

source_observations: T321 and MR-P154 support the established प्रमाण रूप wording; the full Kleene theorem title and exact T/U construction are fixed by OpenLogic.

The source's proof sketch asserts primitive recursiveness of both T and U across the described coding and then states weaker sufficient hypotheses for many applications; the translation keeps this distinction.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
